chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Yahya ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Abi Najran, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever glorifies Allah at the end of the obligatory prayer with the glorification of Fatima al-Zahra (peace be upon her), one hundred times, and follows it with 'La ilaha illa Allah', Allah will forgive him.

key_terms.بِلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: With 'There is no god except Allah'

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Tasbih al-Fatima after prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the unique status of Sayyida Fatima al-Zahra (peace be upon her) by linking her specific litany of glorification to immediate divine forgiveness. In Shia tradition, this practice is not merely a ritual but a means of spiritual purification and attaining closeness to the Ahl al-Bayt, emphasizing the intercessory and exemplary role of the Prophet's daughter in daily worship.
